text.p: Asia-Pacific leaders gathered on Monday for an annual summit to boost plans to create the 21st century's biggest free-trade community.

Leaders from the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum, including U.S. President Bill Clinton, Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, were to meet for a day in this former U.S. naval base 80 km (50 miles) north of the capital Manila.

Secret service agents told reporters that aircraft carrying APEC leaders had flown into Subic Bay airport and the leaders were making their way to the summit centre nearby on a hill overlooking the bay where American Pacific fleets used to shelter.
Over the next six hours, the leaders will discuss in formal and informal sessions how to realise their aim of barrier-free trade in the Asia-Pacific by 2020.

Among other subjects will be a U.S. proposal for eliminating tariffs on information technology products by the turn of the century. The controversial question of China's membership of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) was also likely to come up on the sidelines.

The summit kicked off amid tight security due to fears that leftist groups may mount terror attacks to disrupt the talks. But a demonstration planned by thousands of anti-APEC protesters was called off as the summit got underway.
